subject: Clarify downstream productization & feedback license — Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Monique Rivera <mrivera@edgescale.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jacob Stern <jstern@edgescale.com>, procurement@edgescale.com
Date: 2026-08-22 09:14 -0700
Subject: Order Form redlines — downstream productization + training license

Ben — thanks for the call this morning. We reviewed the latest Order Form and MSA excerpt with our legal team and posted a few redlines (attached PDF). High level asks: 

- EdgeScale needs explicit "output ownership" for any model outputs that are a direct transformation of our customer content (we propose perpetual, worldwide, sublicensable rights for our outputs to productize).
- A carveout to the feedback/training license for any outputs or telemetry that contain customer PII or internal IP. We want an opt-out pathway tracked at the account level (not per-request).
- If Redwood intends to use our data to improve models, we need either an opt-in or an additional commercial term (training opt-out fee).
- Clear attribution/notice language for downstream resellers — we want ability to re-license products that include model-derived outputs.

Attached: EdgeScale_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf. Please advise Redwood's position so we can move to procurement.

Thanks,
Monique
General Counsel | EdgeScale Inc.

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monique Rivera <mrivera@edgescale.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-22 11:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — downstream productization + training license

Monique — really appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. We've reviewed at a high level and want to propose the following approach to keep the deal moving while protecting both sides: 

1) Output ownership: we can agree to grant EdgeScale a broad, non-exclusive license to productize outputs derived solely from EdgeScale-provided customer content. We cannot assign exclusive title to outputs because (a) our models may incorporate general improvements and (b) we have to allow reuse of generic outputs across customers. Proposal: non-exclusive, perpetual, transferable license back to EdgeScale with a productization carveout tied to "Customer Content" as defined in the MSA.

2) Training/feedback: Redwood's standard model-improvement clause is a limited feedback license where we may use anonymized/aggregated telemetry for model tuning. We're open to a stronger opt-out. Options we can offer: 
  - Account-level opt-out (no training) — available but requires a minimal monthly surcharge to offset lost model-improvement economics. See attached fee summary.
  - Data-scoped opt-out for PII/internal IP — we can implement filters and tags but need agreement on definitions and evidence sampling policies.

3) Attribution & downstream resellers: we do not object to reasonable downstream use and re-licensing, provided there is a flow-down disclaimer that our models may have been improved with aggregated feedback; we typically require that any sublicensing recipients agree to Redwood's Acceptable Use Policy.

I'm looping in Laura (legal) and Rishi (sales/ops) to coordinate redline responses. Can Laura confirm whether legal is comfortable with the non-exclusive productization license language and whether the training opt-out fee is an approvable addendum? Rishi — do you want me to propose the opt-out fee numbers to procurement, or should legal structure the counter?

Best,
Ben
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-22 15:37 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order Form redlines — downstream productization + training license

Ben / Rishi — quick legal read. Key points for redline drafting and negotiating posture: 

- Acceptable compromise on output license: non-exclusive, perpetual license back to customer for outputs that are demonstrably derived from Customer Content. We need to add a reasonably objective test (e.g., a reproducibility threshold / prompt-derived match) to avoid claims where outputs are generic model artifacts.
- Training/feedback: prefer account-level opt-out (yes) but only with the opt-out fee framework. Approve fee as a commercial term — product can implement an account flag that toggles telemetry ingestion. Add definition of "Personal Data / PII" referencing Section 2.1 of the MSA and require customer evidence for opt-out eligibility. 
- Telemetry retention & audit: include a 90-day retention baseline for telemetry used for improvement and an audit-rights path for customers to verify that opt-out was honored (redacted logs).
- Attribution/flow-down: require any downstream recipient to accept a flow-down MSA; if EdgeScale refuses, we can allow re-licensing but limit liability and require indemnification for misuse.

Action items (legal): I'll draft pointed redline language for the Order Form and an addendum for the training opt-out fee. Estimated turnaround: 48 business hours.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monique Rivera <mrivera@edgescale.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@edgescale.com
Date: 2026-08-24 17:48 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — downstream productization + training license

Monique — thanks for patience. Attaching Redwood's proposed counter-redlines and a short addendum that lays out the opt-out fee schedule and the operational steps to enact an account-level training opt-out (what we call "Training Opt-Out Addendum"). Highlights: 

- Output license: we propose explicit language granting EdgeScale a non-exclusive, perpetual, worldwide license to Outputs that are a "Direct Transformation" of EdgeScale Customer Content (we define direct transformation and include an examples annex). This preserves Redwood's right to use model outputs elsewhere where they are not demonstrably tied to EdgeScale content.
- Training opt-out: account-level opt-out available; fee tiers outlined by committed monthly usage. Implementation requires a 10-business-day lead time and an annual update window. Fee schedule attached (RDW-training-optout-fee-summary.xlsx).
- PII carveout: we accept a PII carveout but require the customer to designate datasets and provide sampling evidence; our engineering team will run a filter check. We will retain telemetry for 90 days by default and will provide redacted audit logs on request under NDA.
- Downstream licensing: EdgeScale may re-license Outputs; however, we require a flow-down that ensures redistributors accept Redwood's AUP and limitation of liability flow-down. If EdgeScale needs a broader assignment, that will require a separate SOW/fee.

Next steps: 
 1) Laura to upload redline PDF and Training Opt-Out Addendum to the Drive link and share a DocuSign-ready Order Form.
 2) Monique / EdgeScale to confirm whether the chargeable opt-out is acceptable and identify datasets for PII carveout.
 3) Rishi to coordinate procurement terms & finalize PO cadence.

If agreeable, we can schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call Wednesday to finish language.

Regards,
Ben
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_OrderForm_Counter_v1_redlines.pdf; RDW-training-optout-fee-summary.xlsx
